content.overview: BNS s. 57 — Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons. BNS restatement of IPC 117. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 117. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 57 is the rule on “Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons”. The section provides that whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 57 exists so that “Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons” has a closed legal test in Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: The inchoate trio. Abetment now covers extra-territorial aid; conspiracy and attempt sit next to it.

The provision in detail
57. Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A affixes in a public place a placard instigating a sect consisting of more than ten members to meet at a certain time and place, for the purpose of attacking the members of an adverse sect, while engaged in a procession. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 57 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 57 (Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons), Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 57 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 57 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
